items.synthetic_content: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution. In this work we propose the Transformer model architecture based solely on attention mechanisms.
items.query: What architecture is the Transformer model based on?
items.expected_answer: The Transformer architecture relies entirely on self-attention mechanisms without sequence-aligned RNNs or convolutions.

items.synthetic_content: Multi-Head Attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. With a single attention head, averaging inhibits this. In our work we employ 8 parallel attention layers, or heads.
items.query: How many parallel attention layers or heads are used in the work?
items.expected_answer: The model employs 8 parallel attention layers or heads.

items.synthetic_content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory. The parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model, while the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a neural retriever.
items.query: What constitutes the parametric and non-parametric memory in RAG?
items.expected_answer: Parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model, whereas non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia.

items.synthetic_content: We evaluate RAG on a wide range of knowledge-intensive tasks, including Open-Domain Question Answering (Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions), abstractive question answering (MS-MARCO), and Jeopardy question generation.
items.query: Which open-domain question answering datasets were evaluated?
items.expected_answer: The evaluated datasets were Natural Questions, TriviaQA, and WebQuestions.
